blocks.content: Connect an existing Prometheus server so Grafana Cloud can query its metrics. You’ll name the connection, enter its address and authentication, and check that the Prometheus API responds.

blocks.title: Before you begin
blocks.content: Have your Prometheus base URL and any required credentials ready, and sign in with permission to add data sources. The server must be reachable from Grafana Cloud: an address that works only on your laptop or VPN needs Private Data Source Connect (PDC). If you already started a configuration, check for it under **Connections** → **Data sources** before creating another.
Open the data source catalog to begin adding your connection.
Open **Add data source** to start connecting your Prometheus server.
blocks.tooltip: Open the catalog to add your connection.

blocks.content: The catalog is where you choose the service Grafana will query.
Create the Prometheus data source, enter its connection details, and check access to its API.
Select **Prometheus** to create a data source configuration.
blocks.tooltip: Create a connection for querying your metrics.

blocks.content: Name this connection `my-prometheus` so you can find it later.

steps.description: Click **Edit title** to give this connection a recognizable name.

steps.tooltip: Use my-prometheus so the guide can check this connection.
steps.description: Enter `my-prometheus` as the name so you can find this connection later.

blocks.tooltip: Enter the base address reachable from Grafana Cloud, including its protocol.
blocks.content: Enter your Prometheus server’s base URL, including `https://` or `http://` and any required port or path prefix. Use an address reachable from Grafana Cloud; do not append `/metrics` or `/api/v1/query`. Enter your own address in the highlighted field; the guide checks its URL format.

blocks.tooltip: Choose the method your endpoint requires and enter credentials directly in Grafana.
blocks.content: Choose the authentication method your endpoint requires and enter any credentials directly in Grafana. Select **No Authentication** only if your endpoint requires no credentials.
Click **Save & test**. Look for **Successfully queried the Prometheus API.** If the test fails, use the troubleshooting tips below, update the settings, and try again.
blocks.tooltip: Check that the saved connection can query the API.

blocks.content: A successful API check confirms that Grafana can reach your Prometheus server using the saved connection settings.

blocks.title: If the connection test fails
blocks.content:
- Timeout or connection refused: check the hostname, port, and firewall rules; Grafana Cloud must be able to reach the server. For a private endpoint, use the PDC setup guide.
- Unauthorized or forbidden: check the authentication method and credentials expected by this endpoint.
- Not found: check the base URL and any path prefix; remove query or metrics paths.
- Certificate error: check the server certificate and any required CA certificate settings.

After correcting the settings, click **Save & test** again. A successful API check confirms connectivity; it does not guarantee that every metric you expect is available.
